          "text": "# Siamese Twins: A Close Pair in Virgo\n\n*Two spiral galaxies share a name that hints at their appearance. Spotting the resemblance takes dark skies, patience and a telescope.*\n\nIn the spring sky, the Siamese Twins offer a quiet lesson in perspective. NGC 4567 and NGC 4568 are two galaxies seen close together from Earth; in a telescope, their faint light can suggest a pair of overlapping forms. The nickname makes a promise, but not a guarantee: these are subtle targets, and the \u201ctwins\u201d may appear more like a soft patch than two neatly separated spirals.\n\nThe catalog entry for NGC 4567 places it at right ascension 12h 36m 32.7s and declination +11\u00b0 15\u2032 29\u2033 (J2000). It lists the galaxy\u2019s apparent visual magnitude as 11.31 and its angular size as about 3.9 by 2.4 arcminutes.
